title: Full Spec MCP: Hidden Capabilities of the MCP spec — Harald Kirschner, Microsoft/VSCode
talk_summary: Harald Kirschner argues most MCP servers only expose tools and miss the spec's stateful primitives: dynamic discovery, resources, sampling, roots, elicitations, and streamable HTTP. He shows concrete client/server mechanisms for reducing tool overload, returning references instead of blobs, and letting tools ask the client LLM or user for missing input.

takeaways.what_they_do: VS Code lets users select a subset of tools per chat and save reusable tool sets, instead of exposing every tool all the time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: So there's a little tool packer and you can actually reduce down the tools

takeaways.what_they_do: An MCP server can add or remove tools based on current state, so a battle tool appears only when a monster is present.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the tool for battling shouldn't be there when there's no monster

takeaways.technique: Return artifact references, not giant blobs
takeaways.what_they_do: MCP resources let a tool return a file reference or semantic artifact that the LLM or user can follow up on, instead of dumping a huge file into context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: return a reference to the file and that could be something the LM could follow up on

takeaways.technique: Sampling through the client model router
takeaways.what_they_do: MCP sampling lets a server request an LLM completion from the client, so tools can ask for summarization/formatting without hardcoding their own model access.
takeaways.evidence_quote: allows the server to request LLM completions from the client

takeaways.what_they_do: Tools can pause and ask the user directly for concrete missing information instead of forcing a separate chat or guessing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a way for tools to finally reach out back to the user when they need more information

takeaways.technique: Streamable HTTP over SSE for remote MCP
takeaways.what_they_do: Use streamable HTTP for hosted MCP servers to avoid the stateful churn of SSE while still supporting HTTP.
takeaways.evidence_quote: avoiding this really stateful churn on your servers
